record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Variance and CLT for total tree length
record.original_question: Let Λ_n be the total edge length of CTCS(n), the sum of all edge lengths in the continuous-time critical beta-splitting tree on n leaves. Prove that n^{-1} Var(Λ_n) converges to 6/π^2, and prove the corresponding central limit theorem for Λ_n.

evidence.quote: one can consider the length Λn of CTCS(n), that is the sum of edge-lengths.
Open Problem 6. Prove that n−1var(Λn) converges to 6/π2 and that the corresponding CLT holds. (Section 4.5).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Continuous-time critical beta-splitting tree CTCS(n). For each integer m ≥ 2, define the probability distribution on splits {1, 2, …, m−1} by
  q(m, i) = 1 / (h_{m−1} · i(m − i)),  1 ≤ i ≤ m − 1,
where h_{m−1} = 1 + 1/2 + ⋯ + 1/(m−1). Construct a random rooted binary tree with n labeled leaves as follows. Start with the root holding the leaf set {1, …, n}. Recursively, a node currently labeled by a set S with |S| = m ≥ 2 waits an exponential time of rate h_{m−1}, then splits S into two nonempty subsets (S_L, S_R) by choosing |S_L| = i with probability q(m, i) and then picking a uniformly random subset of S of size i to be S_L. These two subsets become the labels of the two children of the node, and the recursive construction continues independently on each child until all subsets are singletons (the leaves). Each edge of the resulting tree is assigned length equal to the holding time at its parent node.

Let Λ_n denote the total edge length of this random tree, i.e. the sum of the lengths of all its edges.

Prove the following:
(a) n^{-1} Var(Λ_n) → 6/π^2  as n → ∞.
(b) There exist deterministic centering and scaling constants under which (Λ_n − E Λ_n) / √Var(Λ_n) converges in distribution to a standard normal random variable.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent follow-up work on the critical beta-splitting tree (e.g. CLTs for leaf heights via contraction and via regenerative compositions) extensively addresses heights of uniform random leaves and joint CLTs for discrete/continuous heights, but no located paper explicitly establishes the variance asymptotic n^{-1} Var(Λ_n) → 6/π^2 together with a CLT for the total edge length Λ_n. The status of this specific open problem could not be definitively verified from the available sources.

status_evidence.title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 6 lists the variance and CLT for Λ_n as unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open problem in the source listing such problems.

status_evidence.title: Some central limit theorems for critical beta-splitting trees
status_evidence.snippet: Derives joint CLTs for the heights L_n and D_n of a uniformly random leaf in the discrete and continuous critical beta-splitting trees.
status_evidence.claim: This follow-up paper addresses CLTs for leaf heights but not the total edge length Λ_n.

status_evidence.title: Critical beta-splitting, via contraction
status_evidence.snippet: Provides an alternative proof of the CLT for the height H_n of a uniformly random leaf.
status_evidence.claim: Focuses on leaf-height CLT, not on Λ_n.
